note:
File: runs/theory-rows/s3k/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (already on disk, 500 rows, one per problem; if it is missing, fetched from S3 into runs/theory-tests/ at the same subpath). The recipe names studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py's score_v3; that script calls rln4_lib.grade_v3(gold, text)['score_v3'], which this script uses on the full text field. The text field begins with the prefilled opening ('... line!

'), so len(text) and f include it. Marker (a) is the first line whose lstrip() begins with the literal 'Answer:' (start = the 'A', end = the '
' or end of text). Marker (b) is the first ' oxed{' (end = after its balanced '}', or end of text). The earlier of the two wins. Rows with no marker are dropped. Early: start/len(text) < 0.5 and len(text) - end > 300, measured in characters. Bootstrap is over the kept marker rows. In a resample a group with no rows gets rate 0, and 0/0 is set to 1.0. +inf is reported if the late rate is 0 (JSON 'Infinity'). refuted_by_met = early group < 15 rows or ratio < 1.3. Ambiguity / alt_measured: the literal 'Answer:' test misses markdown labels such as '**Answer:** 5' or '**Answer**: 5', which the base may write and v3's MARK_V3 also catches. alt_measured also counts those (leading *, _, #, > stripped; 'Answer**:'/'Answer*:'/'Answer__:' allowed). Mid-line 'Answer:' and 'Final Answer:' never count as markers in either reading. The ratio could be wrong if the opening's three prefilled characters shift f, which matters only near 0.5.

Same file, filters, marker and early rule as p1 (literal 'Answer:' reading only). Content: the rest of the line after 'Answer:' for an Answer line, the balanced box contents for a box (if unbalanced: the rest of the text). Final answer = rln4_lib.extract_v3(text)[1]. Rows with None or an all-blank final answer are dropped. Main: same = rln4_lib.grade_v3(gold=final, text='Answer: ' + content)['score_v3']. That runs v3's extraction on the built string, so any text after a newline inside the content is lost, a box inside the content is taken as the box's contents, and norm_v3 plus n13_score.grade compare the two. Alt reading (alt_measured): the equivalence test applied straight to the strings, n13_score.grade(norm_v3(final), norm_v3(content with \( \) \[ \] and surrounding *_ removed)), with no re-extraction. Bootstrap is over the kept rows. If no rows are kept, refuted_without_number(). Otherwise the number is reported with refuted_by_met = kept < 8 or mean < 0.6. Caveat: when the first marker is itself the last candidate (an early box with no later marker), same is 1 by construction. Such a row is early only if more than 300 characters of non-marker text follow it.

Same T1 file. Kept: cap_hit false, n_generated <= 2000 (the field as named; n_generated is n_new + 1 in the rows seen, so the cut sits one token stricter than an n_new cut), v3 score_v3 == 0 recomputed with rln4_lib.grade_v3. Early is as in p1. Rows with no marker are kept as not early. Statistic = early / kept, bootstrapped over the kept rows. refuted_by_met = kept < 8 or share < 0.2. If no rows are kept, refuted_without_number(). Alt reading (alt_measured): the markdown-tolerant 'Answer:' marker described in p1's note.

File: runs/theory-rows/s3k/r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (on disk, 500 rows; fetched into runs/theory-tests/ if missing). Kept: cap_hit false. Marker and early rule as in p1, no grading. Rows with no marker count as not early. Statistic = early / kept, bootstrapped over the kept rows. refuted_by_met = share > 0.15. Alt reading (alt_measured): the markdown-tolerant 'Answer:' marker of p1's note. Caveat: RL may box an intermediate result early, or write several boxes. Under the recipe's definition those count as early markers even though they are not answer commitments, which would push the number up.
